title: Byte by byte
description:
A little-endian computer stores the lowest byte of a number at the lowest address. Write the two directions of that rule for a 32-bit number, using shifts and masks (no pointers yet):

```cpp
std::array<std::uint8_t, 4> toLittleEndian(std::uint32_t value);
std::uint32_t fromLittleEndian(const std::array<std::uint8_t, 4>& bytes);
```

- `toLittleEndian(0x12345678)` gives `{ 0x78, 0x56, 0x34, 0x12 }`: element 0 is the byte that would sit at the variable's address.
- `fromLittleEndian` puts them back together, so `fromLittleEndian(toLittleEndian(x)) == x` for every `x`.
hints: `(value >> 8) & 0xFF` is the second-lowest byte. Shift by `8 * i` for byte `i`.
To rebuild, shift each byte back up by `8 * i` and combine them with `|`. Cast the byte to `std::uint32_t` before shifting.
lessonTitle: Memory Is a Row of Bytes
